note: Adapted from Kemner 1930 (Die Fauna Sumatrensis, Bijdrage No. 66, Termitidae); the original is in German. Except for the fore wing length of 18.00, every other row of the original measurement table (head width, body length and others) is damaged or illegible in the scanned copy and has not been recorded; only the alate is described here, the soldier and worker not being described in this account.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Reddish brown, the head and the posterior abdominal tergites darker, chestnut brown; the underside paler. Wings yellowish brown, the costa, the wing scale and the branches within the cubitus darker. Vestiture sparse but evident. Head oval and thick; the frons slightly concave, with a small transverse groove on each side above the mandibular condyles; the basal half of the postclypeus (clypeobasale) very weakly raised, the apical half (clypeoapicale) bright white; labrum about as long as wide, its anterior margin truncate; compound eyes large, slightly projecting, the ocelli directed obliquely forward and almost touching the compound eyes. Antennae 20-segmented, segments 2, 3 and 4 about equal in length, segment 5 slightly shorter. Pronotum slightly wider than the head, the anterior margin shallowly concave, the posterior margin rounded with a very weak median emargination; margins and disc bearing coarse projecting setae about 0.35 mm long. Wings very long and large: the subcosta of the fore wing extends beyond one third of the wing length, the radius distinctly beyond the middle; the radial sector sends 5 branches to the anterior margin, the first arising about 9 mm from the wing base; the media runs along the radial sector, connected to it in its apical half by 3 small branches, and near the wing apex forked through an anterior branch; the media and the cubitus are connected by a network of small branches; the cubitus lies above the middle of the wing, unpigmented and almost invisible, its first 9 branches darker and clearly discernible. Hind wing slightly shorter than the fore wing; subcosta short, about as long as the wing scale; radius reaching the apical quarter of the wing, the radial sector sending 4 branches to the anterior margin; the media arises from the radial sector before the middle of the wing and is connected to it by two cross-bars; the media is visible only at its base, where there are 6 visible branches and several vestigial ones. Cerci short, conical. Legs stout; the base of the hind tibia distinctly bent, the apex with 3 dark spurs. Measurements (mm): fore wing length (excluding the wing scale) 18.00; the remaining values are damaged in the OCR of the original and are not recorded.
